Witness accuses 'Kishoreganj Razakar' of torturing him, 3 others
2016-11-07T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/city/witness-accuses-kishoreganj-razakar-torturing-him-3-others-1310641

A prosecution witness yesterday testified that Syed Mohammad Hussain alias Hossain, an alleged Nikli Thana Razakar commander of Kishoreganj, detained and tortured him and three others during the Liberation War in 1971.

Kashem Ali of Pukurpar village, also the 20th prosecution witness in the case against Hussain and Muhammad Moslem Pradhan of Kishoreganj, told International Crimes Tribunal-1 that he was released later on condition that he provides information about freedom fighters.

Hussain and Moslem face six charges. Moslem is now in jail and pleads not guilty while Hussain is on

the run. Kashem did not say anything about Moslem.

The 70-year-old witness said Hussain along with four to five Razakars picked up the four of them from their houses and other Razakars confined them at Nikli Police Station and tortured them following Hussain's orders.

When a nearby grocer, Abdul Ali, requested that they be released, Hussain demanded a meal for the Razakars in return, said the witness.

Ali provided Hussain three goats and two and half mounds of rice from their houses, said Kashem.

Later, Hussain released them after they gave an undertaking to provide the information and appear at the station every day, he added.

Afterwards, the 21st witness, Abdul Ali, gave a similar testimony. The three-member tribunal led by Justice Anwarul Haque adjourned proceedings until November 21 after a defence counsel completed cross-examining the two.
